 T h is appeal coming on for orders this day, t h e cou r  following:
 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 03.12.2019 passed by 9th Addl. MACT, Ujjain in Claim Case No.13/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Dinesh vs Sohan Singh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59809874/
1
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the injuries suffered by the appellant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,000/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of Income -Rs.10,000/-
 Medical Expenses -Rs.2,96,700/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.25,000/-
 Special diet -Rs.10,000/-
 Attendant charges -Rs.12,500/-
 --------------------
 TOTAL Rs.3,54,200/-
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
As per the disability certificate issued by the treating doctor, the appellant/injured has suffered 45% disability in relation to his body part.
The Tribunal has committed an error in not applying the multiplier method for calculating the compensation under the head of permanent disability.
The income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.5000/- per month is also on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced.
The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any sum under the head of loss of future prospects.
Hence, prayed for awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the injuries suffered by the appellant, the period of treatment and the disability certificate issued by the treating doctor, in the considered opinion of this Court, the tribunal has committed an error in not applying the multiplier method while calculating the compensation amount.
Considering the medical certificate Ex.P/15, the permanent disability suffered by the appellant is assessed as 15%.

Considering the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled labour for the relevant period, the income of the appellant assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side which is enhanced to Rs.6700/- per month.
To this amount, the future prospects woulb be added at the rate of 40% keeping in view the verdict of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. vs. Pranay Sethi - 2017 ACJ 2700.

sentences.text: Considering the age of the appellant/injured, the proper multiplier applicable in the present case would be 16.

In view of the above, the compensation in the present case is recalculated as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT

Permanent disability -Rs.2,70,144/-
 Medical expenses -Rs.2,96,700/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.25,000/-

Dinesh vs Sohan Singh on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59809874/
2  Special diet -Rs.10,000/-

Attendant charges -Rs.12,500/-
 Loss of income during treatment -Rs.13,400/-
 ------------------
 TOTAL Rs.6,27,744/-
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.6,27,744/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,54,200/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,73,544/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.2 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly.

However, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
